items.diagram_kind: contracted exceptional curve, conormal positivity, negative self-intersection
items.selection_reason: Potential editorial aid: the result relates a contracted curve to its conormal/normal line degrees and self-intersection; a diagram could distinguish these line bundles and signs.
items.concrete_diagram_content_or_checks: For E contracted by f, check deg(O_X(−E)|E)>0, E²=deg(O_X(E)|E)<0, and the inverse normal/conormal degree sign. Do not imply a full negative-definite matrix, which the source explicitly disclaims.

source_lines.42: ([[def-divisor-intersection-number-on-smooth-projective-surface]]), let $Y$ be an integral regular finite-type
source_lines.43: $k$-scheme of pure dimension two, let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a proper birational morphism and let $E\subseteq X$
source_lines.44: be an integral curve with $f(E)$ a single closed point $y\in Y$. Then:
source_lines.46: 1. $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$;
source_lines.47: 2. $\deg_E\bigl(\mathcal O_X(-E)|_E\bigr)>0$, that is, the conormal sheaf of $E$ in $X$ has positive degree on $E$; and
source_lines.48: 3. $E\cdot E<0$; equivalently the normal bundle $\mathcal O_X(E)|_E$ has negative degree.
source_lines.50: No similar statement is proved here for curves not contracted by a birational morphism, and no negative definiteness of the full intersection matrix of a reducible exceptional divisor is claimed.
source_lines.80: 1.1 At every point of $X$ the local ring is a regular local ring and therefore a unique factorization domain, so the height-one prime defining the integral curve $E$ is locally principal and $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor; this proves assertion 1. [F3, F6, F7, F11, given]
source_lines.82: 2.1 The curve $E$ is set-theoretically contained in the fibre $f^{-1}(y)$ over the closed point $y$, so the positive conormal degree lemma applies with $Z=E$, whose only irreducible component is $E$ itself, and gives $\deg_E(\mathcal O_X(-E)|_E)>0$; this is assertion 2. [F4, F9, step 1.1]
source_lines.84: 3.1 The restriction-degree identity gives $E\cdot E=\deg_E(\mathcal O_X(E)|_E)$, and additivity of the degree on inverse invertible sheaves gives $\deg_E(\mathcal O_X(E)|_E)+\deg_E(\mathcal O_X(-E)|_E)=0$; hence $E\cdot E=-\deg_E(\mathcal O_X(-E)|_E)<0$, which is assertion 3 and says that the normal bundle of $E$ has negative degree. [F1, F4, F5, F10, step 2.1]
source_lines.86: 4.1 No statement is made for curves not contracted by a birational morphism, and no negative definiteness of the full intersection matrix of a reducible exceptional divisor is claimed; the Axiom of Choice is inherited from the Euler-characteristic and intersection suppliers. [F2, step 3.1] ∎
